observation.initial_state: A chocolate-coated ice cream bar, tilted slightly left, stands upright on a white tray, clamped at its base by a copper-colored binder clip. A small cream-colored puddle of melted liquid is already pooled beneath the clip at t=0. The background is a white textured wall with a fixed owl logo at bottom right; the camera is stationary.
visible_changes: Early (t=0–1.0 s): the bar, clip, and background hold fixed positions; the cream puddle stays a compact blob mostly to the left of the clip base, with no visible dripping or bar movement.
Middle (t=1.0–1.9 s): the bar remains motionless and the same height/shape; the puddle begins to widen slightly, the liquid edge creeping a little further around the clip.

Late (t=2.0–2.67 s): the cream puddle has visibly spread outward, forming a broader rounded pool extending both left and right of the clip base, while the chocolate surface (condensation droplets and the white notch on the bar's right side) and the bar's tilt/position are unchanged.
Throughout, the change is expansion of the existing puddle rather than translation of any object; no new drops, no bar shrinkage, and no camera pan/zoom are evident.
observation.final_state: The ice cream bar is still upright and stationary in the same spot, held by the copper clip, but the cream-colored melted puddle at its base is larger and more spread out than at the start.
uncertain_details: Whether the bar itself is losing volume/height from melting is not clearly discernible from these frames.
The exact growth rate of the puddle is subtle and could partly reflect lighting/reflection differences rather than true spreading.
No falling droplet or drip event is captured, so the melting mechanism is inferred only from the enlarging pool.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
The images are chronological samples of the exact training clip, not its full source video.
Describe visible initial state, changes over the sequence, final state, and important unchanged
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"initial_state":"...", "visible_changes":["chronological observation with early/middle/late evidence"],
"final_state":"...", "uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English.
